Salesforce (CRM) ended the recent trading session at $185.46, demonstrating a +2.68% change from the preceding day's closing price. This change lagged the S&P 500's 4.73% gain on the day. On the other hand, the Dow registered a gain of 3.01%, and the technology-centric Nasdaq increased by 6.51%.

The customer-management software developer's shares have seen a decrease of 27.34% over the last month, not keeping up with the Computer and Technology sector's loss of 19.48% and the S&P 500's loss of 10.18%.

The upcoming earnings release of Salesforce will be of great interest to investors. The company's earnings report is expected on December 2, 2026. In that report, analysts expect Salesforce to post earnings of $3.43 per share. This would mark year-over-year growth of 5.54%. Meanwhile, our latest consensus estimate is calling for revenue of $11.46 billion, up 11.73% from the prior-year quarter.

Regarding the entire year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates forecast earnings of $16.72 per share and revenue of $46.26 billion, indicating changes of +33.55% and +11.4%, respectively, compared to the previous year.

It is also important to note the recent changes to analyst estimates for Salesforce. These latest adjustments often mirror the shifting dynamics of short-term business patterns. With this in mind, we can consider positive estimate revisions a sign of optimism about the business outlook.

Our research shows that these estimate changes are directly correlated with near-term stock prices. To benefit from this, we have developed the Zacks Rank, a proprietary model which takes these estimate changes into account and provides an actionable rating system.

The Zacks Rank system, stretching from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), has a noteworthy track record of outperforming, validated by third-party audits, with stocks rated #1 producing an average annual return of +25% since the year 1988. Over the past month, there's been no change in the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. Salesforce is currently sporting a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy).

Digging into valuation, Salesforce currently has a Forward P/E ratio of 10.81. This denotes a discount relative to the industry average Forward P/E of 18.96.

One should further note that CRM currently holds a PEG ratio of 0.63. This popular metric is similar to the widely-known P/E ratio, with the difference being that the PEG ratio also takes into account the company's expected earnings growth rate. By the end of yesterday's trading, the Internet - Software industry had an average PEG ratio of 1.15.

Zoom Communications (ZM) came out with quarterly earnings of $1.59 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.49 per share. This compares to earnings of $1.52 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +6.71%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this video-conferencing company would post earnings of $1.5 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.55, delivering a surprise of +3.33%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

Zoom, which belongs to the Zacks Internet - Software industry, posted revenues of $1.29 billion for the quarter ended October 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.92%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.23 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Zoom shares have lost about 5.8% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 1%.

What's Next for Zoom?

While Zoom has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Zoom was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.55 on $1.3 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $6.15 on $5.09 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Key Takeaways

Seven big funds cut or sold their Workday stakes in the quarter ended Sept. 30. Eagle Capital Management still held $1.41 billion of the stock, and Meritage Group sold all of its shares.

Several of the same funds also cut their SAP and Salesforce stakes, and Workday is down 8% since Sept. 30.

Workday trades at under 15x forward earnings, against a five-year average of 35x, and analysts expect its earnings per share to rise every year through January 2029.

The numbers don't back the sellers, and Workday's report in late November will show whether analysts' estimates hold.

Seven big funds sold Workday (WDAY:NASDAQ) stock in the third quarter, and the stock is down 8% since Sept. 30. Their 13Fs for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed between Oct. 23 and Nov. 16, show that each one cut its stake by 29% or more and one sold out, with Workday due to report again in late November.

Eagle cut deep, and Meritage sold every share

The biggest seller in dollars is Eagle Capital Management, a firm that manages $36 billion. It cut its Workday stake by 35% in the quarter, to 7.40 million shares worth $1.41 billion at Sept. 30 prices. That's still 4.3% of its 13F stocks and its ninth-biggest holding.

Meritage Group, which manages $14 billion, went further. At June 30, Workday made up 8% of its 13F stocks: 1.63 million shares worth $200 million. By Sept. 30 it held none. Its latest 13F lists just 13 US stocks, so that was one of its bigger bets.

title: Docusign vs. Figma: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:
Docusign vs. Figma: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
Brendan Coffey, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 23, 2026 at 10:31 AM MST 6 min read
DOCU
FIG
MSFT
SAP
CRM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Software investing often involves choosing between established, profitable leaders and high-growth disruptors. Deciding whether to back Docusign (NASDAQ:DOCU) or Figma (NYSE:FIG) requires weighing mature cash flows against aggressive market expansion.

Docusign transformed how contracts are signed, moving beyond simple digital signatures into end-to-end agreement management. Figma redefined digital product design by enabling real-time collaboration for creative teams directly in the browser. Both companies compete for space in corporate software budgets but offer vastly different financial profiles for investors looking ahead to 2027.

The case for Docusign

Docusign provides intelligent agreement management software to help organizations prepare, sign, and manage contracts. The company serves over 1.8 million customers globally and remains a prominent name among tech stocks. It maintains strategic partnerships with organizations such as Microsoft Corp.(NASDAQ:MSFT), SAP (NYSE:SAP), and Salesforce.com Inc. (NYSE:CRM) to integrate its services.

In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached about $3.4 billion, which represents growth of approximately 8.6% compared to the prior period. The company reported net income of around $329.9 million during this same time frame, demonstrating its ability to maintain profitability while expanding its product suite. This consistent financial performance provides a foundation for the company as it rolls out new agreement management tools.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.1x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio is nearly 0.7x, measuring the ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was about $1.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) accounted for roughly 53.4% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Figma

Figma provides a web-based platform that enables design teams to collaborate on digital products in real time. The company hosts its infrastructure on Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and serves over 16,000 paid customers with substantial annual recurring revenue. It focuses heavily on global expansion, with about 85% of its monthly active users currently located outside the United States.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $1.4 billion, showing robust revenue growth of approximately 44.4% as adoption of its design tools accelerated. However, the company reported a net loss of nearly $562.5 million for this period, reflecting elevated operating costs and investments in new features. This balance of rapid top-line expansion and significant bottom-line losses is characteristic of high-growth software firms in their scaling phase.

Citi slashed its Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) price target by nearly 25% on Monday, warning that sluggish demand for the software giant's core products could outweigh its artificial intelligence ambitions ahead of its upcoming earnings report.

Analyst Tyler Radke lowered his target to $198 from $263 while maintaining a Neutral rating, implying approximately 9.6% upside from Friday's closing price of $180.62.

The downgrade in expectations follows Citi's checks with Salesforce customers and partners, which suggest demand for traditional customer relationship management software remains weak.

The bank sees limited evidence that Salesforce's AI products can meaningfully accelerate companywide growth in the near term.

That raises questions about Agentforce, Salesforce's platform for deploying AI agents capable of handling customer service, sales and other business tasks.

Although AI remains central to CEO Marc Benioff's strategy, investors are increasingly focused on whether customer interest translates into substantial recurring revenue.

Salesforce shares have fallen approximately 20% in November, underperforming a broader rebound in software stocks earlier this month.

Investors Takeaway

Citi expects Salesforce to report fiscal third-quarter adjusted earnings of $3.38 per share on approximately $11.5 billion in revenue.

The upcoming report will test whether AI adoption is strengthening enough to offset slower growth in established software products.

Investors should watch subscription revenue, customer spending trends and management's commentary on Agentforce adoption.

The bigger question is whether Salesforce can convert its AI investments into faster growth before competitive pressures further weaken its core business.

title: Is Microsoft Stock Stronger Than It Looks?
detail:
Is Microsoft Stock Stronger Than It Looks?
Trefis Team

MSFT
NVDA
^GSPC
GOOG
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Reported SEC Probe: Could Nvidia Stock Fall To $92?

Microsoft (MSFT) holds a pile of commercial contracts that customers have signed but that it has not yet counted as revenue. Management says it is building its data centers against a growing book of business. Many investors still see that building as a costly bet on AI. Microsoft stock has done little to change that view, returning 0.5% over the past year against 5.3% for the S&P 500. The signed contracts keep growing, but the share price has not followed. So how big has that pile of signed contracts become?

Microsoft's Signed Contracts Are Almost Twice A Year's Sales

At the end of September, customers had signed $677 billion of commercial contracts. Microsoft has yet to count them as revenue. The total was up 73% from a year earlier. The whole company reported $346 billion of revenue over the past twelve months, so the contracts come to almost twice that. Management expects roughly 30% of them to become revenue in the next 12 months. The rest lies further out, and that later part grew 98% from a year earlier.

Most of Microsoft's $677 billion in signed contracts will turn into sales after the next 12 months. If you hold Microsoft for that payoff, your money may need to earn income while you wait. The Trefis Income Solution pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's, from 50 companies that have paid dividends for at least 10 years in a row. See what it pays.

Sales are already moving the same way. Azure revenue grew 48% in fiscal Q1 2027, the quarter ended September 30, 2026. On the call, management said customer demand continues to exceed available supply. So the buildout has customers lined up behind it.

Free Cash Flow Has Fallen As Microsoft Builds

Free cash flow over the past twelve months was $60.0 billion, down from $78.0 billion in the twelve months to September 2025. Capital spending, including finance leases, reached $45.2 billion in fiscal Q1 2027, mostly on short-lived assets such as CPUs and GPUs. Microsoft expects to spend more than $50 billion in fiscal Q2 2027. That rising bill is what worries a holder.

The signed contracts are Microsoft's case for that bill. Microsoft says it is building against a growing book of business, and the signed contracts are the clearest measure of that book. Cash is coming in faster too. Cash from operations rose 29% to $58 billion in fiscal Q1 2027, on strong cloud billings and collections.

Still, free cash flow fell even as the contracts grew. Microsoft also said it will tap other sources of funding when it finds them attractive. In late October 2026, a source said Microsoft expected to raise $25 billion in a US bond sale.

The best way to find great value stocks is to pair a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system. The proven Zacks Rank emphasizes companies with positive estimate revision trends, and our Style Scores highlight stocks with specific traits.

Salesforce has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), while Adyen N.V. Unsponsored ADR has a Zacks Rank of #4 (Sell) right now. This means that CRM's earnings estimate revision activity has been more impressive, so investors should feel comfortable with its improving analyst outlook. But this is just one piece of the puzzle for value investors.

Value investors analyze a variety of traditional, tried-and-true metrics to help find companies that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

The Value category of the Style Scores system identifies undervalued companies by looking at a number of key metrics. These include the long-favored P/E ratio, P/S ratio, earnings yield, cash flow per share, and a variety of other fundamentals that help us determine a company's fair value.

CRM currently has a forward P/E ratio of 10.81, while ADYEY has a forward P/E of 20.38. We also note that CRM has a PEG ratio of 0.63. This popular figure is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also considers a company's expected EPS growth rate. ADYEY currently has a PEG ratio of 1.43.

Another notable valuation metric for CRM is its P/B ratio of 3.87. The P/B is a method of comparing a stock's market value to its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, ADYEY has a P/B of 5.08.

Based on these metrics and many more, CRM holds a Value grade of A, while ADYEY has a Value grade of D.

CRM is currently sporting an improving earnings outlook, which makes it stick out in our Zacks Rank model. And, based on the above valuation metrics, we feel that CRM is likely the superior value option right now.
